name: Punt expedition of Sahure
description: 5th-Dynasty Egyptian seaborne expedition to Punt recorded in Sahure's mortuary temple reliefs; scholars debate whether it was tribute exchange or armed campaign.

name: Hatshepsut's expedition to Punt
description: Hatshepsut's celebrated naval expedition to Punt, documented at Deir el-Bahari, included a military escort but is mostly characterised as commercial.

name: Egyptian campaigns into Wawat
description: Old Kingdom Egyptian raids and campaigns of Weni and Harkhuf into Wawat (Lower Nubia) for stone, slaves and tribute.

name: Egyptian campaigns against Yam
description: Harkhuf's four expeditions from Aswan deep into Yam in Upper Nubia, recorded in his autobiographical tomb inscription.

name: Senusret III's Nubian campaigns
description: Senusret III's four invasions of Nubia fixed the Egyptian frontier at Semna and built the chain of Second Cataract fortresses.

name: Kerma's invasions of Upper Egypt
description: Kerma raids into Upper Egypt during the Hyksos period, attested in the Elkab tomb inscriptions of Sobeknakht.

name: Thutmose I's Nubian campaign
description: Thutmose I sacked Kerma and pushed the Egyptian frontier to the Fourth Cataract at Kurgus.

name: Kushite conquest of Egypt
description: Piye and Shabaka's Kushite invasion that founded the 25th Dynasty of black pharaohs ruling all Egypt and Nubia.

name: Assyrian conquest of Egypt
description: Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal expelled the Kushite 25th Dynasty from Egypt, ending Nubian rule of the Nile valley.

name: Psamtik II's Nubian campaign
description: Saite Egyptian expedition deep into Kush that sacked Napata and is recorded in Greek graffiti at Abu Simbel.

name: Roman-Kushite War
description: Kandake Amanirenas led the Meroitic invasion of Roman Egypt; Petronius's counter-strike sacked Napata before the Treaty of Samos fixed the frontier.

name: Aksumite conquest of Meroë
description: Ezana of Aksum's campaign across the Atbara recorded on his stelae effectively ended the Meroitic kingdom of Kush.

name: Aksumite invasion of Himyar (GDR)
description: GDRT and his successor ʿDBH led the first attested Aksumite crossings of the Bab al-Mandab to fight in South Arabia.

name: Aksumite expedition of Sembrouthes
description: Aksumite king Sembrouthes claimed victory in South Arabia in his Adulis inscription.

name: Aksumite invasion of Himyar (Kaleb)
description: Kaleb of Aksum's invasion overthrew the Jewish Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas after the Najran massacre, installing the viceroy Sumyafa Ashwa.

name: Abraha's expedition against Mecca
description: Abraha's elephant-led march on Mecca, defeated by plague according to Surat al-Fil, traditionally dated to the Year of the Elephant.

name: Sasanian conquest of Yemen
description: Sasanian general Vahrez expelled the Aksumite garrison from Yemen at the invitation of Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan.

name: Aksum–Beja conflicts
description: Recurring Aksumite campaigns against the Beja tribes of the Red Sea Hills, attested in the inscriptions of Ezana and Kaleb.

name: Aksum–Noba war of Ezana
description: Ezana's Greek and Geʽez stelae record his campaign against the Noba people who had overrun former Kushite territory.

name: Aksum–Agaw wars
description: Long Aksumite frontier wars against the Agaw highlanders to the south, leading to gradual assimilation.

name: Arab–Aksumite raids
description: Aksumite raid on Jeddah (702) provoked the Umayyad seizure of the Dahlak archipelago, ending Aksumite Red Sea maritime power.

name: Bantu expansion into the Great Lakes
description: Centuries-long Bantu-speaking migration into the African Great Lakes, displacing earlier Twa and Cushitic populations; rarely framed as a single named war but is the demographic substrate of later interlacustrine politics.

name: Battle of Embabo
description: Menelik of Shewa defeated Tekle Haymanot of Gojjam, settling Shewan control of the Oromo lands west of the Abay.

name: Zagwe–Solomonic transition wars
description: Yekuno Amlak's revolt overthrew the last Zagwe king Yetbarak and founded the Solomonic dynasty in Ethiopia.

name: Amda Seyon's campaigns
description: Amda Seyon's chronicled campaigns subjugated Ifat, Hadiya, Damot and Gojjam, fixing the medieval Christian Ethiopian frontier.

name: Ifat–Ethiopian wars
description: Century of Walashma–Solomonic warfare ending when Dawit I and Yeshaq I crushed Saad ad-Din II of Ifat at Zeila.

name: Battle of Zeila (1415)
description: Yeshaq I of Ethiopia killed the Walashma sultan Saad ad-Din II at Zeila, scattering the Ifat royal house.

name: Adal–Ethiopian wars (pre-Gragn)
description: Century of frontier raiding between the Solomonic emperors and the Walashma successors at Dakkar and Harar, climaxing in the regency of Sabr ad-Din.

name: Battle of Gomit
description: Zara Yaqob's heavy victory over Sultan Badlay of Adal at Gomit secured the eastern frontier for two generations.

name: Ethiopian–Funj border wars
description: Recurring frontier conflict between Gondarine Ethiopia and the Funj Sultanate of Sennar across the western lowlands.

name: Hadiya wars under Zara Yaqob
description: Zara Yaqob's campaigns against the Hadiya Sultanate brought the Sidama south firmly under Christian Ethiopian overlordship.

name: Ethiopian–Adal War (Futuh al-Habasha)
description: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi (Gragn) overran most of Christian Ethiopia until a Portuguese musketeer expedition under Cristovão da Gama and the death of Gragn at Wayna Daga reversed the tide.

name: Battle of Shimbra Kure
description: Imam Ahmad Gragn's first decisive victory over Emperor Dawit II opened Ethiopia to Adal conquest.

name: Battle of Amba Sel
description: Gragn's victory at Amba Sel scattered the last large Ethiopian field army and led to the looting of Lalibela and Aksum.

name: Battle of Wofla
description: Adal-Ottoman forces defeated and captured Cristovão da Gama, who was executed by Imam Ahmad.

name: Battle of Wayna Daga
description: Emperor Gelawdewos and the Portuguese survivors killed Imam Ahmad Gragn in battle, breaking Adal's invasion of Ethiopia.

name: Oromo migrations
description: Successive luba-led Oromo gadaa expansions described in Bahrey's Zenahu la Galla, transforming the political geography of the Horn after the Gragn wars.

name: Battle of Hazalo
description: Emperor Gelawdewos was killed in battle against Nur ibn Mujahid of Harar at Hazalo.

name: Ottoman–Ethiopian War (1557–1589)
description: Özdemir Pasha's seizure of Massawa, Arqiqo and Debarwa created the Habesh Eyalet; Sarsa Dengel finally drove the Ottomans back to the coast at Addi Qaro.

name: Battle of Addi Qaro
description: Emperor Sarsa Dengel destroyed the Ottoman-supported Bahr Negash Yeshaq at Addi Qaro, restoring Ethiopian control of the highlands.

name: Susenyos's wars against the Oromo
description: Emperor Susenyos waged a long war against the Tulama and Macha Oromo, eventually settling many as soldiers in his service.

name: Ethiopian Catholic civil war
description: Susenyos's conversion to Catholicism triggered an Orthodox revolt under his son Fasilides that ended with the expulsion of the Jesuits.

name: Mombasa rebellion (1631)
description: Sultan Yusuf ibn al-Hasan massacred the Portuguese garrison at Fort Jesus before being expelled the following year.

name: Omani–Portuguese War on the Swahili coast
description: Ya'rubid Omani fleets progressively expelled the Portuguese from the Swahili coast, climaxing in the siege of Fort Jesus.

name: Siege of Fort Jesus
description: Three-year Omani siege ended Portuguese rule on the Swahili coast north of Cape Delgado.

name: Capture of Mombasa (1729)
description: Brief Portuguese reconquest of Mombasa during a Swahili revolt against Oman, lost again the following year.

name: Battle of Sagallo
description: French naval bombardment dispersed Nikolai Achinov's short-lived Cossack colony at Sagallo on the Tadjoura coast.

name: Funj–Ethiopian War (1730s)
description: Emperor Iyasu II's Sennar campaign was defeated at the Dinder River, fixing the Ethio–Sudan frontier for a century.

name: Zemene Mesafint
description: "Era of the Princes" — eighty years of warlord rule in which Yejju Oromo regents at Debre Tabor controlled the puppet Gondarine emperors.

name: Buganda–Bunyoro wars
description: Two-century rivalry between the Great Lakes kingdoms in which Buganda gradually displaced Bunyoro-Kitara as the dominant interlacustrine power.

name: Mwanga I of Buganda's wars
description: Eighteenth-century Bugandan wars of expansion under Mawanda and Junju into Buddu and Busoga at Bunyoro's expense.

name: Nyamwezi caravan wars
description: Nineteenth-century conflicts among Nyamwezi chiefs, Arab caravan traders and the Mirambo confederation along the central caravan route to Lake Tanganyika.

name: Battle of Magdala
description: Napier's punitive expedition stormed Tewodros II's fortress of Magdala; the emperor shot himself rather than surrender.

name: British Expedition to Abyssinia
description: Robert Napier's 1867–68 expedition from Annesley Bay to Magdala to free European hostages held by Emperor Tewodros II.

name: Battle of Gundet
description: Yohannes IV annihilated Werner Munzinger's Egyptian column at Gundet on the Mareb.

name: Battle of Gura
description: Yohannes IV destroyed the second and larger Egyptian invasion army under Ratib Pasha at Gura.

name: Ethiopian–Egyptian War
description: Khedive Isma'il's invasion of northern Ethiopia ended in two crushing defeats at Gundet and Gura.

name: Mahdist War in Ethiopia
description: Yohannes IV's wars against the Sudanese Mahdists climaxed in his death at the Battle of Gallabat/Metemma in March 1889.

name: Battle of Gallabat
description: Yohannes IV of Ethiopia was killed at the moment of victory over the Mahdist army at Gallabat.

name: Italian conquest of Eritrea
description: Italian seizure of Massawa, defeat at Dogali (1887) and final occupation of the highlands that created the colony of Eritrea.

name: Battle of Dogali
description: Ras Alula annihilated a 500-man Italian column under De Cristoforis at Dogali, an early checkpoint on Italy's path to Adwa.

name: Battle of Coatit
description: Oreste Baratieri repulsed Ras Mengesha Yohannes at Coatit early in the First Italo-Ethiopian War.

name: Battle of Amba Alagi (1895)
description: Ras Makonnen overwhelmed Major Toselli's Italian rearguard at Amba Alagi, prompting the Italian retreat to Adigrat.

name: Siege of Mekele
description: Menelik II's army forced the surrender of Major Galliano's Italian garrison at Enda Yesus on the eve of Adwa.

name: Battle of Adwa
description: Menelik II's decisive victory destroyed Baratieri's Italian army, securing Ethiopia's independence and ending the First Italo-Ethiopian War.

name: Menelik II's southern conquests
description: Menelik II's expansion roughly doubled the size of the Ethiopian Empire through campaigns against Arsi, Kaffa, Welayta, Sidama and the Ogaden.

name: Battle of Chelenqo
description: Menelik's army crushed Emir Abdullahi II at Chelenqo, annexing the Emirate of Harar to Ethiopia.

name: Arsi Oromo wars
description: Menelik II and Ras Darge's repeated campaigns ending at the Battle of Azule incorporated the Arsi Oromo into Shewa.

name: Welayta War
description: Menelik II's army subdued King Tona Gaga of Welayta and incorporated the southern kingdom into Ethiopia.

name: Kaffa War
description: Ras Wolde Giyorgis's troops captured King Gaki Sherocho, ending Kaffa as an independent kingdom.

name: Battle of Anchim
description: Ras Tafari's loyalists defeated and killed Ras Gugsa Welle, removing the last serious obstacle to Haile Selassie's accession.

name: Italian invasion of Somalia
description: De Vecchi's Campaign of the Sultanates ended the autonomy of Hobyo and Majeerteen and consolidated Italian Somaliland.

name: Anglo-Sudan Mahdist War
description: Muhammad Ahmad's jihad against the Turco-Egyptians and then the Anglo-Egyptian reconquest under Kitchener, ending at Omdurman.

name: Fall of Khartoum
description: The Mahdi's army stormed Khartoum and killed General Gordon two days before the British relief force arrived.

name: Battle of Omdurman
description: Kitchener's Anglo-Egyptian army annihilated the Khalifa Abdullahi's Mahdists, completing the Anglo-Egyptian reconquest of Sudan.

name: Battle of Atbara
description: Kitchener's victory over Emir Mahmud at Atbara opened the Nile road to Omdurman.

name: Battle of Toski
description: Egyptian forces under Grenfell smashed Wad an-Najumi's Mahdist invasion of Egypt at Toski.

name: Anglo-Egyptian conquest of Sudan
description: Kitchener's three-year reconquest of the Mahdist Sudan culminating in Omdurman and the destruction of the Khalifa at Umm Diwaykarat.

name: Battle of Umm Diwaykarat
description: Reginald Wingate killed the Khalifa Abdullahi at Umm Diwaykarat, formally ending the Mahdist state.

name: Fashoda Incident
description: Anglo-French confrontation at Fashoda on the White Nile, resolved diplomatically in Britain's favour.

name: Anglo-Sudanese campaigns against the Beja
description: Osman Digna's Hadendoa forces fought British expeditionary columns at El Teb, Tamai and Tofrek along the Red Sea coast.

name: Anglo-Buganda war (1892)
description: Lugard's Maxim-gun intervention at Mengo decided the Buganda religious civil war for the Anglican faction.

name: Buganda religious wars
description: Three-way Bugandan civil war between Muslim, Catholic and Protestant chiefs that drew in the IBEACo and eventually produced the British Protectorate.

name: Bunyoro resistance under Kabarega
description: Kabarega and the exiled Kabaka Mwanga II waged a six-year guerrilla war against the Anglo-Bugandan column until their capture at Lango.

name: Lango campaign (1901)
description: British pacification campaigns against Lango and Acholi chiefs in northern Uganda.

name: Nandi Resistance
description: Eleven-year resistance of the Nandi orkoiyot Koitalel arap Samoei against British incursions and the Uganda Railway.

name: Giriama Uprising
description: Mekatilili wa Menza's revolt against British labour and tax demands in coastal Kenya.

name: Abushiri Revolt
description: Swahili-Arab planter Abushiri ibn Salim led a coastal revolt against the German East Africa Company, suppressed by Hermann von Wissmann's mixed Sudanese-Zulu force.

name: Hehe Wars
description: Chief Mkwawa's seven-year Hehe resistance, including the destruction of Zelewski's column at Lugalo (1891) and ending with Mkwawa's suicide.

name: Battle of Lugalo
description: Mkwawa's Hehe ambushed and destroyed Emil von Zelewski's Schutztruppe column at Lugalo.

name: German campaigns against the Chagga
description: Schutztruppe campaigns under Carl Peters and Hermann von Wissmann against Mandara and Sina of the Chagga chiefdoms.

name: Maji Maji Rebellion
description: Pan-tribal revolt of southern Tanganyika against the cotton scheme; suppressed by famine campaigns that killed perhaps 200,000.

name: Battle of Mahenge
description: German garrison's machine-gun defence of Mahenge broke the largest Maji Maji frontal assault.

name: East African Campaign (World War I)
description: Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck's four-year guerrilla campaign across German East Africa, Mozambique and Northern Rhodesia.

name: Battle of Tanga
description: Lettow-Vorbeck's Schutztruppe routed Aitken's Indian Expeditionary Force B at Tanga ("Battle of the Bees").

name: Battle of Jassin
description: German victory over a Punjabi-Anglo column on the Kenyan border.

name: Kilimanjaro Campaign
description: Smuts's offensive captured the German position around Kilimanjaro and opened German East Africa.

name: Battle of Mahiwa
description: Bloodiest engagement of the East African campaign; Lettow-Vorbeck inflicted heavy losses on a Nigerian brigade before retreating into Mozambique.

name: Battle of Negomano
description: Lettow-Vorbeck destroyed the Portuguese garrison at Negomano and crossed into Mozambique to continue the war.

name: Anglo-Somali War (Dervish State)
description: Twenty-year struggle between the British and Mohammed Abdullah Hassan's Dervishes, ended by the 1920 RAF bombing of Taleh.

name: Battle of Jidballi
description: Egerton's force broke the Dervish concentration at Jidballi, forcing the Mad Mullah into the Italian Mijirteyn.

name: Battle of Dul Madoba
description: Dervish ambush wiped out Richard Corfield's Somaliland Camel Constabulary column.

name: RAF Somaliland campaign
description: Three weeks of RAF bombing destroyed the Dervish fortress at Taleh and ended Hassan's twenty-year rebellion.

name: Sayyid Hassan Bardera campaigns
description: Early Dervish campaigns into Ethiopia and southern Somalia before the 1904 Jidballi defeat.

name: Italian invasion of Ethiopia (1935)
description: Mussolini's invasion across the Mareb and from Italian Somaliland that ended in Badoglio's entry into Addis Ababa.

name: Battle of Amba Aradam
description: Italian use of poison gas and mass air bombardment destroyed Ras Mulugeta's army on Amba Aradam.

name: Battle of Maychew
description: Final pitched battle of the Second Italo-Ethiopian War, where Haile Selassie's Imperial Guard was destroyed by Italian gas and air attack.

name: Battle of Shire
description: Italian victory over Ras Imru Haile Selassie on the western front of the Second Italo-Ethiopian War.

name: Battle of the Ogaden (1936)
description: Graziani's southern Italian columns broke Ras Nasibu's army at the Battle of Genale Doria and overran the Ogaden.

name: Yekatit 12 massacre
description: Three-day Italian reprisal massacre after the attempted assassination of Viceroy Graziani killed perhaps 19–30,000 Ethiopians.

name: Ethiopian Patriots resistance
description: Five-year Arbegnoch ("Patriots") guerrilla war that kept Italian East Africa under siege until the British liberation campaign.

name: East African Campaign (World War II)
description: Anglo-Commonwealth–Ethiopian Patriot offensive that destroyed Italian East Africa in less than a year.

name: Italian conquest of British Somaliland
description: Italian forces under Guglielmo Nasi forced the only British colonial-territory loss of WWII at Tug Argan and Berbera.

name: Battle of Keren
description: Two-month British–Indian–Free French battle through the Dongolaas Gorge broke Italian Eritrea's defences.

name: Battle of Gondar
description: Final Italian East African pocket at Gondar surrendered to Anglo-Ethiopian forces in November 1941.

name: Battle of Amba Alagi (1941)
description: Duke of Aosta's surrender at Amba Alagi essentially ended Italian East Africa.

name: Gideon Force / Gojjam campaign
description: Orde Wingate's small Gideon Force escorted Haile Selassie back from Khartoum and unhinged the Italian position in Gojjam.

name: Woyane Rebellion
description: Tigrayan peasant revolt against re-imposed Shewan rule, crushed with RAF air support on the eve of the post-war era.

name: Bale revolt
description: Seven-year Oromo–Somali peasant insurgency in Bale led by Waqo Gutu, the first sustained Oromo armed movement.

name: Mau Mau Uprising
description: Kikuyu-led Land and Freedom Army insurgency in central Kenya and its violent suppression in the Aberdares and the colonial detention camps.

name: Shifta War
description: Kenyan Somali secessionists supported by Mogadishu fought to join the NFD to Greater Somalia.

name: Zanzibar Revolution
description: Field Marshal Okello's revolt overthrew the Arab sultanate and led to the union with Tanganyika; 5–20,000 Arabs and Indians killed.

name: East African mutinies (1964)
description: Simultaneous mutinies of the Tanganyika, Uganda and Kenya Rifles, suppressed by British Royal Marines and 45 Commando.

name: Rwandan Revolution
description: Hutu "social revolution" overthrew the Tutsi monarchy of Kigeli V, sending tens of thousands of Tutsi into exile.

name: Inyenzi raids
description: Tutsi exile guerrillas ("cockroaches") launched cross-border raids from Burundi, Uganda and Tanganyika, prompting massacres of Tutsi inside Rwanda.

name: Bugesera invasion (1963)
description: Tutsi inyenzi raid from Burundi sparked the Gikongoro massacre of 10–14,000 Tutsi inside Rwanda.

name: Burundi crisis of 1965
description: Failed Hutu officers' coup followed by massacres of Hutu politicians and intellectuals.

name: Ikiza (1972 Burundi genocide)
description: Tutsi-led army massacred 100–300,000 Hutu after a southern Hutu uprising — the first acknowledged genocide in independent Africa.

name: 1993 Burundi coup
description: Assassination of President Melchior Ndadaye triggered Hutu reprisals and the Burundian Civil War.

name: Genocide of Tutsi in Rwanda
description: Hundred-day genocide that killed about 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu, ended by the RPF's capture of Kigali.

name: Tanzania–Uganda War
description: Nyerere's invasion in response to Amin's annexation of the Kagera Salient overthrew the Amin regime.

name: Operation Entebbe
description: Israeli commando hostage rescue at Entebbe Airport during the Amin regime.

name: Ugandan Bush War
description: Yoweri Museveni's National Resistance Army guerrilla war that overthrew the Obote II and Okello regimes from the Luwero Triangle.

name: War in Uganda (1986–1994)
description: Successive northern Ugandan insurgencies (UPDA, Holy Spirit Movement under Alice Lakwena, UPA) against the Museveni government.

name: Holy Spirit Movement insurgency
description: Alice Auma Lakwena's prophetic insurgency that marched on Jinja before being crushed by the NRA at Magamaga.

name: Allied Democratic Forces insurgency
description: ADF Islamist insurgency in the Rwenzori border region, since 2019 affiliated to the Islamic State Central Africa Province.

name: Eritrean War of Independence
description: Thirty-year war ending with the EPLF capture of Asmara on 24 May 1991 and de facto Eritrean independence.

name: Battle of Afabet
description: EPLF's destruction of three Ethiopian divisions at Afabet, called by Basil Davidson the largest victory by African guerrillas since Dien Bien Phu.

name: Operation Fenkil
description: EPLF's combined-arms capture of the port of Massawa cut off the Ethiopian Second Army in Eritrea.

name: Tigray People's Liberation Front insurgency
description: TPLF guerrilla war that, in alliance with the EPLF, ultimately captured Addis Ababa and overthrew the Derg in May 1991.

name: Ethiopian Red Terror
description: Derg campaign of urban repression that killed perhaps 30–500,000 alleged opponents.

name: Ethio-Somali War (1964)
description: Two-week border war over the Ogaden ended by OAU mediation.

name: Western Somali Liberation Front insurgency
description: Somali ethnic insurgency in the Ogaden that catalysed and outlasted the 1977 conventional war.

name: Ogaden War
description: Siad Barre's invasion of the Ogaden defeated by a Cuban-Soviet counter-offensive at Jijiga and Harar.

name: Battle of Jijiga
description: Soviet–Cuban-led counter-offensive recaptured Jijiga from the Somali army, breaking the Ogaden invasion.

name: Somali Rebellion
description: Multi-clan insurgency that destroyed the Barre regime and triggered the collapse of the Somali state.

name: Isaaq genocide
description: Barre's bombing and ground campaign against the Isaaq killed an estimated 50–200,000 people.

name: Battle of Mogadishu (1993)
description: Task Force Ranger's botched arrest of Aidid lieutenants, dramatised as "Black Hawk Down," ended American direct involvement in UNOSOM II.

name: Ethiopian intervention in Somalia
description: Ethiopian invasion that ousted the Islamic Courts Union from Mogadishu and triggered the al-Shabaab insurgency.

name: Eritrean–Ethiopian War
description: Two-year border war over Badme that killed perhaps 100,000 and produced the Algiers Agreement.

name: Battle of Badme
description: Ethiopian "Operation Sunset" breakthrough at Badme in February 1999.

name: Djibouti–Eritrea border conflict
description: Border clashes around Ras Doumeira ended by the 2018 Eritrea–Djibouti rapprochement after Qatari peacekeepers withdrew.

name: FRUD insurgency
description: Afar-led FRUD insurgency against Issa-dominated Djiboutian government, ended by power-sharing.

name: First Sudanese Civil War
description: Anyanya separatist war in southern Sudan ended by the Addis Ababa Agreement of 1972.

name: War in Darfur
description: Sudanese government and Janjaweed campaign against the SLA and JEM that killed perhaps 200–400,000 and displaced 2.7 million.

name: Sudanese conflict in South Kordofan and Blue Nile
description: Post-independence SPLM-North insurgency in the Two Areas, often called the "third Sudanese civil war."

name: Sudan civil war (2023–)
description: SAF–RSF war that has produced what the UN calls the world's largest displacement crisis.

name: South Sudanese Civil War
description: Kiir–Machar split detonated five years of ethnically targeted warfare that killed perhaps 400,000.

name: Heglig Crisis
description: Two-week war between Sudan and South Sudan over the Heglig oilfield, ended by AU mediation.

name: Lord's Resistance Army insurgency
description: Joseph Kony's millenarian Acholi insurgency that displaced 1.7 million Ugandans and spread into the DRC, CAR and South Sudan.

name: Kenyan intervention in Somalia (Linda Nchi)
description: Kenyan Defence Forces invasion of southern Somalia that captured Kismayo from al-Shabaab.

name: Westgate shopping mall attack
description: Four-day al-Shabaab siege of the Westgate Mall in Nairobi.

name: Garissa University attack
description: Al-Shabaab massacre of 148 students at Garissa University College.

name: Insurgency in Cabo Delgado spillover
description: Northern Mozambique jihadist insurgency that has drawn Tanzanian and Rwandan military intervention.

name: Ethiopian Tigray War
description: Two-year war between the federal government with Eritrean and Amhara allies and the TPLF, ended by the Pretoria Agreement.

name: Battle of Mekelle (2020)
description: ENDF capture of the Tigrayan capital that opened the Tigray War.

name: Operation Alula
description: TDF counter-offensive that retook Mekelle in June 2021 and forced an ENDF withdrawal from most of Tigray.

name: War in Amhara
description: Insurgency by Amhara Fano militias against the federal government after the 2023 dissolution of regional special forces.

name: Oromo Liberation Army insurgency
description: Long-running OLA insurgency in Oromia, intensified after the 2018 split with the OLF.

name: Gambella conflict
description: Recurrent ethnic conflict in Gambella, beginning with the 2003 Anuak massacre.

name: M23 rebellion (Rwanda-DRC)
description: Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebel offensive in eastern DRC, an East African dimension of the broader Kivu conflict.

name: Lake Cyohoha massacres
description: Tutsi army massacres of Hutu peasants around Lake Cyohoha during the Ikiza.

name: Mengistu's Red Star Campaign
description: Soviet-backed multi-divisional Derg offensive against the EPLF's Nakfa redoubt, defeated after six months.

name: Battle of Karamarda
description: Somali Army's breakthrough at the Karamarda Pass opened the road to Harar early in the Ogaden War.

name: Acholi-Buganda war (1893–94)
description: Anglo-Bugandan column under Colvile pushed Kabarega's Banyoro into Acholiland during the conquest of Bunyoro.

name: Ankole–Bunyoro wars
description: Two centuries of intermittent warfare between the Hima kingdoms of Ankole (Nkore) and Bunyoro-Kitara.

name: Karagwe–Buganda wars
description: Recurrent wars across Lake Victoria's west between Karagwe and the expanding Buganda kingdom.

name: Mirambo's wars
description: Nyamwezi chief Mirambo's wars built a short-lived Tabora-Urambo empire that contested Arab caravan routes.

name: Ngoni invasions of East Africa
description: Ngoni offshoots of the Mfecane raided across the East African Rift, settling among the Yao, Bena and Hehe.

name: Sayyid Said's wars on the Swahili coast
description: Sayyid Said's expeditions broke the Mazrui hold on Mombasa and consolidated Omani authority on the Swahili coast.

name: Mazrui revolts
description: Century of Mazrui resistance to Omani Busaidi rule in Mombasa, ending with the fall of Fort Jesus in 1837.

name: Bushiri's Pangani campaign
description: Coastal phase of the Abushiri Revolt centred on the Pangani river, ended by Wissmann's amphibious assault.

name: Wahehe campaigns
description: Sustained Schutztruppe campaign that destroyed Mkwawa's Kalenga fortress and tracked him until his 1898 suicide.

name: Wabena wars
description: Pre-colonial conflicts among the Bena, Hehe and invading Ngoni on the Tanzanian highlands.

name: Mau Mau detentions and Hola massacre
description: Beating to death of eleven Mau Mau detainees at Hola Camp helped end the Kenya Emergency.

name: South Sudan Equatoria insurgency
description: Equatorian-led insurgent groups (NAS under Thomas Cirillo) waged a parallel war against Juba after the 2016 collapse of the peace agreement.

name: Da'amat-Saba war
description: Possible conflicts between the Sabaean-influenced kingdom of Da'amat in Tigray and South Arabian Saba, attested only fragmentarily.

name: Aksumite expedition to Saba
description: GDRT's intervention in the Sabaean civil war recorded in South Arabian inscriptions naming the negus and his son Beygat.

name: Zanj Rebellion (Iraq)
description: Massive revolt of East African (Zanj) slaves in the Abbasid salt marshes of southern Iraq; included here as the largest East African-diaspora war of the medieval era.

name: Sailors of Oman in Pemba and Lamu
description: Arab and Persian colonisation of the northern Swahili coast attested at Shanga, Manda and Pemba — only intermittently a military process.

name: Kilwa civil war (Mahdali takeover)
description: Yemeni Mahdali dynasty seized Kilwa from the Shirazi line, beginning the city's golden age under al-Hasan ibn Talut.

name: Mogadishu–Kilwa trade war
description: Long contest between Mogadishu and Kilwa for control of the Sofala gold trade, eventually won by Kilwa.

name: Yekuno Amlak's wars
description: Yekuno Amlak's revolt from Shewa overthrew the last Zagwe king Yetbarak and founded the Solomonic dynasty.

name: Yagbe'u Seyon's wars
description: Second Solomonic emperor's campaigns against the Walashma of Ifat, opening four centuries of Christian–Muslim frontier war.

name: Battle of Das
description: Amda Seyon's victory over Sabr ad-Din of Ifat as chronicled in his royal Glorious Victories.

name: Dawit I's campaigns
description: Emperor Dawit I campaigned deep into Ifat and crossed the Red Sea to threaten Mamluk Egypt over Coptic patriarchs.

name: Yeshaq I's Adal war
description: Yeshaq I killed Sa'ad ad-Din II at Zeila and pursued the Walashma to extinction; the dynasty later regrouped as Adal at Dakkar.

name: Zara Yaqob's Adal wars
description: Emperor Zara Yaqob's campaigns against Sultan Badlay ibn Sa'ad ad-Din II and the Gibe sultanates secured a generation of peace.

name: Mahfuz's jihads
description: Emir Mahfuz of Harar's annual Lenten jihads against Ethiopia, killed by Lebna Dengel in 1517, foreshadowed Gragn's wars.

name: Pate–Faza wars
description: Centuries of Lamu Archipelago wars among the Nabhani sultans of Pate, Faza, Siyu and Lamu, recorded in the Pate Chronicle.

name: Battle of Shela
description: Lamu's victory over a Pate–Mazrui invasion fleet at Shela; its appeal for protection brought Omani Busaidi rule to the Lamu Archipelago.

name: Portuguese sack of Mombasa (1505)
description: Francisco de Almeida's fleet stormed and burned Mombasa on the first Portuguese reconnaissance of the Swahili coast.

name: Portuguese sack of Kilwa (1505)
description: Almeida built the Gereza fort and installed a Portuguese puppet sultan at Kilwa, beginning Lusitanian rule on the Swahili coast.

name: Sack of Mombasa (1528)
description: Nuno da Cunha's second Portuguese sack of Mombasa.

name: Battle of Mombasa (1589)
description: Portuguese fleet trapped Mir Ali Bey's Ottoman corsair squadron at Mombasa while the cannibal Zimba sacked the city from the landward side.

name: Mir Ali Bey's expeditions
description: Two Ottoman corsair expeditions down the Swahili coast that nearly detached the northern city-states from Portugal.

name: Zimba raids
description: Cannibal warband from the Zambezi sacked Kilwa and Mombasa before being annihilated at Malindi by Segeju levies.

name: Anglo-Zanzibar War
description: 38-minute Royal Navy bombardment that deposed Sultan Khalid bin Barghash, often called the shortest war in history.

name: Wadai expedition (Rabih)
description: Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr's army carved a Sudanese-Saharan empire from Bahr el Ghazal to Bornu before its destruction at Kousseri.

name: Belgian conquest of Rwanda
description: Belgian Force Publique occupied Ruanda-Urundi during the WWI East African Campaign, beginning Belgian rule.

name: Battle of Tabora
description: Belgian Force Publique captured Tabora, headquarters of German East Africa's central railway.

name: Yao slaving wars
description: Yao slave-raiding wars between Lake Nyasa and Kilwa, an East African endemic conflict that drew in British anti-slavery patrols.

name: Anglo–Egyptian Suakin campaign
description: British and Indian columns at Suakin tried to keep open a route to relieve Khartoum.

name: Konso–Borana conflicts
description: Pre-conquest Konso–Borana skirmishing along the southern Ethiopian highland edge.

name: Battle of Korem (1989)
description: TPLF victory at Inda Aba Guna near Korem cleared Tigray of Derg forces.

name: EPRDF capture of Addis Ababa
description: TPLF-led EPRDF entered Addis Ababa on 28 May 1991, ending the Ethiopian Civil War.

name: Battle of Asmara (1991)
description: EPLF entry into Asmara on 24 May 1991 marked de facto Eritrean independence.

name: Operation Restore Hope
description: US-led UNITAF intervention to secure famine relief in Somalia, precursor to UNOSOM II.

name: Battle of Baidoa (2006)
description: Ethiopian-backed TFG forces repelled the ICU attack on Baidoa, opening the December 2006 Ethiopian intervention.

name: AMISOM offensive against al-Shabaab
description: AU peace-enforcement mission's offensives that pushed al-Shabaab out of Mogadishu (2011) and Kismayo (2012).

name: Anuak massacre
description: Killing of about 400 Anuak in Gambella town by Ethiopian troops and highlander militias in December 2003.
